note: Leighton captures a standing man stretching, with both arms bent beside his head. The relaxed gesture lengthens the torso while shifting the body off its central axis. This scan was made at the Royal Academy of Arts in London. The medium and dimensions of this captured version have not been verified.
attribution: The Sluggard by Frederic, Lord Leighton. Royal Academy of Arts. 3D scan by Beto88, via Polycam, CC BY 4.0. Atrium repackaged and Draco-compressed the geometry and reduced textures to 2048-pixel WebP images; triangle count unchanged.

title: Aphrodite Removing Her Sandal
year: Second half of the 2nd century CE
scan_source: Photogrammetric model of the physical sculpture, preserved in the openly licensed Objaverse archive. Browser geometry optimized from that exact source.
note: Aphrodite balances on one leg to remove a sandal before bathing. The small marble turns undressing into a sculptural problem of support and balance. Traces of paint survive on its surface.
attribution: Aphrodite Removing Her Sandal. Artwork: Unknown Roman sculptor. 3D model: Badisches Landesmuseum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Atrium derivative: geometry optimized for browser display. The optimized model and rendered derivative are distributed under the same CC BY-SA 4.0 license.

title: Aurore (Les Vagues)
scan_source: Photogrammetric scan of the physical sculpture; browser geometry optimized from the openly licensed source. The scan predates the museum’s 2022 repair of cracks and a nose.
note: Two adult female figures lean together in a close embrace. Carved from local Sarrailh stone and inspired by the poetry of Francis Jammes, this work stands at the entrance to the Musée de Guéthary. Its intertwined bodies invite a curatorial reading of intimacy between women, without fixing a single narrative or claiming a documented lesbian subject.
attribution: Aurore (Les Vagues). Artwork: Georges-Clément de Swiecinski (1878–1958). 3D model: pattarrian; CC BY 4.0. Atrium derivative: geometry optimized for browser display.
